examples.en: That actor has a sophisticated, city-like image.
This cafe has an urbane, stylish atmosphere.
Her outfit is urbane, so it stands out.
Even though he is from the countryside, his way of speaking is urbane.
The room decorated in an urbane style is very neat.
It is a design that stands out for its urbane sense.

explain: 사람, 옷차림, 분위기가 세련되고 도시 사람 같을 때 칭찬하는 느낌으로 써요. '도시적'과 비슷하지만 도회적은 세련된 이미지가 더 강해요. 반대 느낌은 '소박하다', '시골스럽다'예요.

phrases.en: This outfit has an urbane feel.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도회적'은 '-인' 꼴로 명사를 꾸밀 때 가장 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: '도회적' is most natural in the '-인' form before a noun.

phrases.en: My older sister has a sophisticated, city-like look.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서술어로 쓰면 사람이 세련되어 보인다는 칭찬이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a predicate, it praises someone for looking sophisticated.

phrases.en: It's a building with an urban design.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도회적'과 비슷하지만 세련됨보다 도시다운 모습에 초점이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but focuses more on looking like a city than on sophistication.

explain_en: It is used with a complimentary feel for a person, outfit or atmosphere that looks refined and like a city dweller. It is close to '도시적', but 도회적 has a stronger image of sophistication. The opposite feeling is '소박하다' or '시골스럽다'.

examples.en: The books are lined up neatly on the bookshelf.
The child's handwriting is neat and straight, so it's easy to read.
I walked along the straight, orderly road.
The desks in the classroom look lined up in neat rows.
I feel good when the inside of the closet is neatly arranged.
It is a village known for its neatly squared fields.

explain: 여러 개가 모두 곧고 바르게 정돈된 모습에 써요. '반듯하다'는 하나의 물건이나 사람의 행실이 바를 때도 쓰지만, '반듯반듯하다'는 여러 개가 줄지어 있을 때 잘 어울려요. 반의어는 '삐뚤빼뚤하다'예요.

phrases.en: I stacked the documents neatly and straight.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여 여러 개를 가지런히 두는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-게', it describes arranging many items neatly in order.

phrases.en: I wrote the letter in neat, straight handwriting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글자 여러 개가 가지런할 때 잘 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A good pairing when many letters are written evenly.

phrases.en: The line wasn't straight, so we lined up again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 정돈이 안 된 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, describing something that isn't tidy or aligned.

explain_en: It describes many things that are all straight and neatly arranged. '반듯하다' can also be used for a single object or a person's proper behavior, but '반듯반듯하다' fits best when many things are lined up. The opposite is '삐뚤빼뚤하다' (crooked).

en: to be noisy; to be flashy; to be making a fuss

examples.en: The kids are running around noisily, so it's loud.
I woke up startled by the loud racket.

examples.ko: 결혼식을 너무 요란스럽지 않게 하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to have a wedding that isn't too flashy.

examples.ko: 왜 이렇게 요란스러워요? 조금만 조용히 해 주세요.
examples.en: Why are you making such a fuss? Please be a bit quieter.
The outfit was so loud that everyone stared.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 개업 행사를 요란스럽게 했어요.
examples.en: That shop held a lavish, noisy opening event.

explain: 소리가 시끄러울 때뿐 아니라 옷차림, 행사, 색깔이 지나치게 화려하고 눈에 띌 때도 써요. '요란하다'와 쓰임이 가까워요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '요란스러워요', '요란스러운'으로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: The street is so noisy and flashy today.
phrases.nuance_en: The 해요체 form, where ㅂ changes to 워.

phrases.en: I stood out because of my flashy outfit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷이 지나치게 화려할 때 명사를 꾸미는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for clothes that are overly flashy.

phrases.en: We kept the wedding small and not showy.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form means quiet and modest.

explain_en: It is used not only for loud noise but also for outfits, events or colors that are overly flashy and attention-grabbing. Its usage is close to '요란하다'. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '요란스러워요' and '요란스러운'.

examples.ko: 나무 밑에 개미가 우글우글 모여 있어요.
examples.en: Ants are gathered in swarms under the tree.

examples.ko: 휴가철 공항에 사람들이 우글우글 몰려 있어요.
examples.en: People are crowded together at the airport in the holiday season.
The fish in the tank are swarming around.

examples.ko: 쓰레기통 주변에 벌레가 우글우글 있어서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled because bugs were swarming around the trash can.
Kids gathered in crowds at the amusement park.

examples.ko: 우글우글 모여 있는 비둘기를 피해서 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked around the pigeons flocked together.

explain: '우글우글 + 모이다/몰리다/있다'처럼 쓰고, 우글거리는 모양을 나타내요. 사람이 많을 때는 '바글바글'도 비슷하게 자주 말해요. 벌레나 동물이 모여 있는 모습에도 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The weekend market is packed with people.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우글우글'과 비슷하지만 사람이 많은 곳에 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but used more often for crowds of people.

phrases.en: Customers crowd in on the first day of the sale.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한꺼번에 많이 모여드는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes many coming together all at once.

phrases.example: 풀밭에 작은 벌레가 우글우글 기어 다녀요.
phrases.en: Small bugs crawl around in swarms on the grass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌레나 동물이 많이 움직이는 모습에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits insects or animals moving in large numbers.

explain_en: It is used like '우글우글 + 모이다/몰리다/있다' to show the swarming look. For lots of people, '바글바글' is also often used in a similar way. It suits scenes of bugs or animals huddled together.
